repo.description: ### Summary Dokploy 0.29.13 Drop deployments extract attacker-supplied ZIP entries under an application code directory, but the path validation only checks that the resolved path remains under Dokploy's global base path. As a result, a member user assigned to one application can upload a ZIP entry such as: ```text ../../../traefik/dynamic/member-drop-hijack.yml ``` The entry escapes the assigned application's code directory and writes a global Traefik dynamic configuration file. In my proof, that file defines a higher-priority router for another hostname. Traefik loads the written file and routes traffic for the victim hostname to the attacker's backend. ### Details Relevant source locations in Dokploy 0.29.13: - `packages/server/src/utils/builders/drop.ts:24`: the expected extraction base is `//code`. - `packages/server/src/utils/builders/drop.ts:56`: the ZIP entry name becomes `filePath`. - `packages/server/src/utils/builders/drop.ts:68`: `fullPath = path.join(outputPath, filePath)`. - `packages/server/src/utils/builders/drop.ts:69`: validation calls `readValidDirectory(fullPath, application.serverId)`. - `packages/server/src/wss/utils.ts:47-55`: `readValidDirectory` checks containment under global `BASE_PATH`, not under the application code directory. - `packages/server/src/utils/builders/drop.ts:98`: the ZIP entry is written to `fullPath`. The validation prevents escaping out of `/etc/dokploy`, but it does not prevent escaping from one application's code directory into sibling Dokploy-managed areas such as `/etc/dokploy/traefik/dynamic`. This is not a Docker mount feature or an expected file-publishing behavior. The proof writes a global reverse-proxy routing file outside the member's assigned application directory and changes routing for another hostname. ### PoC Use the attached PoC: - `poc/drop_zip_traefik_hijack_probe.py` Run: ```bash python poc/drop_zip_traefik_hijack_probe.py ``` The PoC sets up two local backend containers and a local Traefik instance using Dokploy's dynamic configuration directory. The sequence is: 1. A victim router initially routes `victim.example.test` to the victim backend. 2. A default member assigned to one application uploads a Drop ZIP with a traversal entry targeting the global Traefik dynamic config directory. 3. The uploaded file defines a higher-priority router for the same hostname. 4. Traefik loads the new dynamic file. 5. Requests for the victim hostname are routed to the attacker's backend. Observed result: ```text scope=Dokploy v0.29.13 official release image attacker_role=default member assigned to one application operator_config_verdict=no unsafe setting; Drop deployment and Traefik file provider are standard Dokploy paths pre_write_http_status=200 pre_write_victim_marker_present=True pre_write_marker_present=False drop_upload_status=200 written_global_config_present=True post_write_http_status=200 post_write_victim_marker_present=False post_write_marker_present=True post_write_body='DOKPLOY_DROP_TRAEFIK_ROUTING_HIJACK' traefik_loaded_router=True verdict=cross_service_routing_hijack_confirmed ``` Expected result: Drop ZIP extraction should reject entries that escape the assigned application's code directory. Actual result: The ZIP entry is accepted, a global Traefik dynamic config file is written, and routing for another hostname is hijacked. ### Impact A member with access to one application can write outside that application and modify global Traefik dynamic routing configuration. This can redirect traffic for another service or hostname to an attacker-controlled backend. Depending on deployment topology, this may expose credentials, sessions, service traffic, or cause service integrity and availability impact. ### Attachments - `poc/drop_zip_traefik_hijack_probe.py` - `poc/traefik-owner-victim.yml` - `evidence/evidence_run.txt` - `screenshots/drop_before.png` - `screenshots/drop_after.png` [drop_zip_traefik_hijack_probe.py](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/30334276/drop_zip_traefik_hijack_probe.py) [traefik-owner-victim.yml](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/30334282/traefik-owner-victim.yml) [evidence_run.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/30334294/evidence_run.txt)
repo.summary: Dokploy Drop deployment ZIP traversal can overwrite global Traefik dynamic routing configuration
